steps.summary: Text reading 'KENT' engraved in stone decorative element at the top center of the building facade
Partially visible Latin text reading 'IVS EST ARS' and additional text below the arched doorway
Two fluted Ionic columns with spiral volutes supporting the facade, painted white or light gray
Neoclassical stone facade with decorative moldings and dentil pattern running horizontally at the top
Red brick wall construction visible between and around the architectural elements
Arched black iron-framed doorway at the center of the facade with fan-light above the arch
Three large rectangular sash windows with multiple panes arranged horizontally above the main entrance
Multiple decorative rectangular panels in stone or light-colored material flanking the central entrance on either side
Rusticated stone quoins and voussoirs framing the arched entranceway
White barrier or fence visible at the bottom left of the image near ground level
Small rectangular white signboard or placard visible on the left side near ground level

The engraved 'KENT' (e1) and Latin motto 'IUS EST ARS BONI ET AEQUI' (e2, meaning 'Law is the art of the good and the equitable', a common legal/courthouse motto) strongly suggest this is a courthouse in a county named Kent. The neoclassical facade with Ionic columns (e3, e4, e6-e9) is typical of American county courthouses. A 'Book Return' sign is also visible near the entrance, suggesting this may actually be a library rather than courthouse - possibly the Kent County Public Library. Given the combination of 'KENT' and courthouse-style architecture with a book return, this is likely a courthouse or civic building in a Kent County, most probably Chestertown, Maryland, the seat of Kent County, Maryland.
